Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a prominent opacity in the right apical region (indicated by the arrow) with associated destruction/erosion of the adjacent ribs, which is characteristic of a Pancoast tumour (superior sulcus tumour). This diagnosis aligns with the patient's history of long-term smoking and symptoms of disorientation (likely due to hypercalcemia from squamous cell carcinoma or brain metastases).
